title: OrderBy Shuffle & Executor OOM
learningOutcome: Postmortem a failed nightly sorted export: explain why orderBy + coalesce(1) + collect_list under 512m executor memory OOMs

questions.prompt: On a 10k-row sample this job finishes. On the full drop it dies under the same 512m executors. What does that pattern tell you about where the plan’s cost actually lives?
choices: The code path must be different at full scale — Spark silently rewrites orderBy into collect() only when the input is large
Correctness is fine either way; failure means MinIO rejected a large write, not that executor work grew with the input

The expensive work is proportional to how much data must be shuffled, sorted, gathered into one partition, and held in an in-heap structure — a sample never stresses the same per-task working set as the full drop on a tiny heap
Full-scale runs always use the driver for sorting; samples stay on executors, so only production hits driver OOM
questions.correctAnswer: The expensive work is proportional to how much data must be shuffled, sorted, gathered into one partition, and held in an in-heap structure — a sample never stresses the same per-task working set as the full drop on a tiny heap
questions.explanation: orderBy + coalesce(1) + collect_list do more memory-heavy executor work as the input grows. A sample can hide a plan that cannot fit the real working set in 512m.

questions.prompt: Trace the exhibit: orderBy → coalesce(1) → agg(collect_list(struct(...))) → collect. A coworker says “just bump driver memory — sorts always happen on the driver.” Why is that the wrong mental model for this failure?
choices: They are right for DataFrame orderBy; only RDD sort runs on executors
Driver memory only affects UI; Spark never uses the driver heap for anything in a write job
The shuffle/sort, the single-partition gather, and the collect_list buffer all run as executor work — the 512m worker heap is what has to hold that array, not the driver’s 1g
coalesce(1) moves the entire dataset to History Server, so neither driver nor executor memory matters
questions.correctAnswer: The shuffle/sort, the single-partition gather, and the collect_list buffer all run as executor work — the 512m worker heap is what has to hold that array, not the driver’s 1g
questions.explanation: collect_list here builds an unbounded array inside an executor task. Raising driver memory does not enlarge the worker that is dying with Java heap space.

questions.prompt: A streaming orderBy write can often spill sort buffers to disk and survive. Why does this exhibit’s coalesce(1) + collect_list path remove that escape hatch on a 512m executor?
choices: coalesce(1) disables Tungsten and forces every row through Python on the driver
coalesce(1) puts the whole ordered stream in one task, and collect_list must retain every element in that task’s JVM heap — there is no spill path for an unbounded aggregation buffer
collect_list only runs on the driver; coalesce is irrelevant
orderBy already cached the data on disk, so collect_list is free
questions.correctAnswer: coalesce(1) puts the whole ordered stream in one task, and collect_list must retain every element in that task’s JVM heap — there is no spill path for an unbounded aggregation buffer
questions.explanation: External sort can spill; collect_list cannot. One task holding every sorted row as an array is a hard heap cliff.

questions.prompt: Open the frozen History Server app for this exhibit. Which reading of the failure actually matches how this plan runs?
choices: Application SUCCEEDED but OUTPUT_PATH is empty — grading failed, not Spark
A failed stage/task while building the single-partition collect_list, with ExecutorLostFailure / Java heap space (or container OOMKilled) — a worker died under memory pressure
Only the driver shows OutOfMemoryError while every executor stage is green — classic broadcast build failure
No jobs appear because orderBy is lazy and write never scheduled
questions.correctAnswer: A failed stage/task while building the single-partition collect_list, with ExecutorLostFailure / Java heap space (or container OOMKilled) — a worker died under memory pressure
questions.explanation: Local Docker rehearsal showed repeated `OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` on the collect_list stage, then lost executors. History should tell that same story.
questions.historyHint: Application status → failed stage/task error details

questions.prompt: On-call proposes four fixes. Which one actually confronts the root cause of this incident?
choices: Rename appName and rerun — History Server was caching the old OOM
Keep coalesce(1) + collect_list and only raise spark.driver.memory so the “sort node” has room

Change the contract or the plan: drop the single-file funnel and the unbounded in-heap collect_list, avoid a global sort unless the loader truly needs total order, and/or size executor memory for the real per-task working set
Replace collect_list with collect_set — sets always spill automatically under 512m
questions.correctAnswer: Change the contract or the plan: drop the single-file funnel and the unbounded in-heap collect_list, avoid a global sort unless the loader truly needs total order, and/or size executor memory for the real per-task working set
questions.explanation: Root cause is plan + resources: global order + one partition + unbounded aggregation buffer on a 512m trail. Driver-only memory or renaming the app does not remove that cliff.
